findings.comment: No title commitment, title policy, Ownership and Encumbrance Report, or ALTA/ACSM boundary survey has been submitted to Austin Energy for review. UCM § 1.16.0(1) requires these documents for all sites with electric easements to verify adequacy of existing easements and identify conflicts.

applicableAreas: Site plan sheets; particularly electrical design plan sheets
findings.comment: Electric easements are shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan) with recording references, but presence cannot be verified on Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan). Applicability requirement states easements must be shown on all site plan sheets for Austin Energy facilities. Metes and bounds descriptions and field notes exhibits required by UCM § 1.16.0(1)(i) are not provided.

applicableAreas: North, East, and South property boundaries; areas within 5-foot electric easements
findings.comment: Landscape plan (Sheet 31) proposes extensive tree plantings (M-mitigation trees) and sod groundcover extending to North, East, and South property boundaries where 5-foot electric easements exist. No license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement is documented or referenced on the plans. License agreements are required before installing landscaping or trees within electric easement areas.

Note stating Austin Energy has the right to prune and remove trees and vegetation per LDC Chapter 25-8, Subchapter B is present on Sheet 3 but missing from Cover Sheet. This note must appear on the cover sheet as a required plan note.

Note requiring owner to provide Austin Energy with easements and access for installation and maintenance of electric facilities without site non-compliance is present on Sheet 3 but missing from Cover Sheet. This note must appear on the cover sheet.

applicableAreas: Grading Plan; southwest corner near existing overhead lines and proposed retaining wall
findings.comment: Grading plan (Sheet 11) proposes significant fill and retaining wall work (TW 682.23-684.43) along southern property boundary where existing overhead electric lines are located (Sheet 4). Proposed grades are 4-6 feet higher than existing terrain (~678), reducing clearances to overhead lines. No note on Grading Plan addresses owner responsibility for costs if final grades do not meet required clearances. This note must appear on the grading plan.

Note stating owner is responsible for maintaining clearances required by NESC, NEC, OSHA, City rules, and Texas state laws when working near overhead lines, and that Austin Energy will not render service unless clearances are maintained is present on Sheet 3 but missing from Cover Sheet. This note must appear on the cover sheet.
